summary: Read the control receipt (896586fa6bf04a74877fe81547c2599f, completed, tests_passed, exit 0, no changed target files), which carries the finding and its control in one invocation: indices 0-2 are the explicit-transition case (joint admission with voters [1 2 3 4] against outgoing [1 2 3]; the proposal step returning no error and leaving an EntryConfChangeV2 with its payload intact, so validation accepted it; apply panicking with config is already joint while still joint), and indices 3-4 are the Auto-transition control (LeaveJoint true, EnterJoint ok false, no panic, joint configuration left with voters [1 2 3 4]), with both control comparisons holding and complete. I also discovered that my earlier interpretation for this investigation had never been recorded - the saved state listed no interpretation for it - so this submission records it now: a measured fact tied to indices 1, 2 and 4, and an interpretation with conclusion holds and defect claim asserted. The finding: propose-time validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes) == 0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition, so an empty ChangeV2 with an explicit transition is accepted and replicated as an EntryConfChangeV2 and then panics the process in the application's ApplyConfChange call, whereas the not-joint case is rejected with a log message and an entry rewrite; the control shows the issue is specific to the transition field, and an application that rejects the change instead of applying it can avoid the crash, which is why the claim is scoped to the acceptance-then-panic inconsistency and no state corruption or safety violation is claimed.
